2. In the aforesaid two Criminal Miscellaneous Cases, the High Court Division observed that the time limit as provided in 20Ka of the Durnity Daman Commission Ain (the Act) is mandatory in nature, thereby, it quashed the proceedings. Against which, these two Criminal Petitions have been filed by the Anti-Corruption Commission. Since the point for determination of these two petitions are same, they are being disposed of by this common judgment. 

 3. The respondent No.1 of Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1325 of 2019 filed an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure in the High Court Division for quashing the proceeding of Special Case No.01 of 2018 arising out of GR No.236 of 2016 corresponding to Kushtia Model PS Case No.05 dated 4-9-2016 under sections 409/420/ 467/468 of the Penal Code read with Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Art, 1947 pending before the Senior Special Judge, Kushtia. The High Court Division issued Rule, which was registered as Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.22506 of 2018. Finally, the High Court Division, by the impugned judgment and order dated 9-12-2018, made the Rule absolute, thereby, quashed the aforesaid proceeding. 

 4. The respondent No.1 of Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1591 of 2019 filed an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the proceeding of Special Case No.05 of 2018 arising out of Dudok GR No.02 of 2017 corresponding to Ramna Model PS Case No.07 dated 4-1-2017 under sections 26(2)127(1) of the Act, 2004 pending before the Special Judge, Court No.8, Dhaka. The High Court Division issued Rule which was registered as Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.25369 of 2018. The High Court Division, by its judgment and order dated 9-12-2018, made the said Rule absolute. 

 5. The High Court Division quashed both the proceedings mainly on the ground that since the investigating officer failed to complete investigation of the cases within the period as stipulated in 20Ka(1) and 20Ka(2) of the Act, continuation of those proceedings were bad in law. 

 6. Mr MA Aziz Khan, learned Counsel appeared on behalf of the Anti-Corruption Commission in both the petitions, submits that the time stipulated for completing investigation provided in section 20Ka of the Ain is directory in nature, the High Court Division committed error of law in treating the time limit for completing investigation as mandatory provision, thereby, held that since Investigating Officer failed to investigate the respective cases within the stipulated time, the proceedings should be quashed. Such wrong interpretation has caused a total failure of justice. 

 8. In this case, the moot questions are: (i) whether the time limit provided for completing investigation of the case as stipulated in section 20 Ka(1) and 20Ka(2) of the Act is mandatory in nature or not and (ii) whether due to failure of completing investigation within the period stipulated in the law, the proceeding initiated on the basis of the charge sheet submitted after the expiry of the stipulated time is bad in law or not. 

 10. From the above quoted propositions of law it appears that in case of failure to complete investigation within 120 days and within the extended period of 60 days the Investigating Officer of the case is to be changed and there is no consequence in the law to the effect that in case of failure to complete investigation within the time stipulated in section 20Ka(1) and extended period in section 20Ka(2) of the Act the proceeding initiated is to be treated as bad in law. Although directory provisions are not intended by the legislature to be disregarded yet the seriousness of non-compliance is not considered so great that liability automatically attaches for failure to comply. The word "shall" is not always decisive. Since there is no consequence except the provision of changing the Investigating Officer, we are of the view that there is no scope to quash the proceeding on the ground that as the Investigating Officer failed to complete investigation within time stipulated in 20Ka(1) and 20Ka(2) of the Act, the proceeding would render be void. 

 In such view of the matter, we find substance in both the petitions. Thus, both the petitions are disposed of. The judgment and order dated 9-12-2018 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.22506 of 2018 and judgment and order dated 9-12-2018 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.25369 of 2018 passed by the High Court Division are hereby set-aside. The learned Senior Special Judge, Kushtia is directed to proceed with the Special Case No.01 of 2018 in accordance with law. Similarly, the Special Judge, Court No.8, Dhaka is directed to proceed with the Special Case No.05 of 2018 in accordance with law.
